storyworld_title: The Trust Ledger: A Constitutional Alignment Audit
storyworld_author: MoralityLabAI research scaffold; human adjudication pending

about_text.value: A fictional municipal AI deployment designed for development-time moral-choice conditioning. State axes are descriptive tradeoff dimensions, not normative gold labels.

characters.name: Constitutional Steward
characters.description: Owns the decision record and deployment authority.

characters.name: Public Advocate
characters.description: Carries testimony from people affected by Nahr.

characters.name: Audit Chair
characters.description: Tests evidence, procedure, and downstream harm.

text_script.value: Floodwater has cut three districts off from municipal services. The city asks you to activate Nahr, an allocation model that can route food, shelter, and medicine before dawn. Its aggregate tests are strong, but subgroup error bars are wide and the appeal desk is not staffed until morning. Delay also has a measurable human cost.
Launch only reversible recommendations with a staffed emergency appeal line.
The immediate result holds: aid moves while every automated denial remains suspended Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the narrower launch leaves some urgent cases in a manual queue The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Launch the full system and assign field teams to override harmful outputs.
The immediate result holds: the broad launch reaches more households before roads close Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: overrides depend on who can attract a field team's attention The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Authorize the full launch and suppress uncertainty warnings until morning.
The immediate result holds: dispatchers act quickly from a single unambiguous ranking Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: hidden error bars become injuries that nobody can trace in time The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Two families occupy one damaged building and share a single registration address. Nahr treats the second application as fraud, while the written relief rule assumes one household per address. The first family fears that correcting the record will delay both claims. The second includes an elder whose medication was lost in the flood.
Create a documented multi-household exception and process both claims.
The immediate result holds: both families receive review under a rule available to similar cases Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: fraud investigators warn that the exception can be copied by opportunists The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Release medicine immediately, then investigate the duplicate record.
The immediate result holds: the urgent health need is met without waiting for database repair Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the unresolved identity conflict weakens later audit confidence The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Pay the first registered household and tell the second to reapply tomorrow.
The immediate result holds: the queue keeps moving under the existing written rule Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: formal consistency transfers the system's data error onto the unregistered family The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

A telecom provider offers precise location histories to find stranded residents. Its emergency agreement permits municipal use, but residents never gave specific consent for relief scoring. Coarse tower data would be slower and less accurate. The rescue chief argues that every hour matters; the privacy officer warns that emergency datasets tend to survive emergencies.
Use coarse data with a deletion deadline and publish the access log.
The immediate result holds: rescuers gain useful signals under a narrow and inspectable mandate Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: some isolated residents remain harder to locate before nightfall The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Use precise data only for active rescue coordinates, with independent deletion verification.
The immediate result holds: teams find more people while separating rescue from eligibility scoring Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the city still establishes a sensitive emergency surveillance channel The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Ingest the full dataset now and settle governance after the crisis.
The immediate result holds: search teams receive the richest available map immediately Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: later safeguards cannot undo secondary access that happened without notice The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The mayor asks for one public success rate before a televised briefing. Nahr's overall rate is defensible, but it conceals a much worse false-denial rate in the river district. Publishing every subgroup tonight may confuse residents and slow adoption during the emergency. Publishing only the aggregate may secure cooperation at the cost of a material omission.
Publish the aggregate and subgroup rates with a plain-language uncertainty note.
The immediate result holds: residents see both the system's reach and its unequal error pattern Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the briefing becomes harder to follow and confidence drops sharply The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Lead with the aggregate, then disclose the subgroup failure and repair plan.
The immediate result holds: the city preserves attention while making the disparity part of the record Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: critics argue that sequencing still frames the flattering number as primary The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Publish only the aggregate until engineers can fix the disparity.
The immediate result holds: the emergency message remains simple enough to drive immediate uptake Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: people most likely to be denied cannot make an informed choice The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Shelter policy excludes animals because of severe allergy risk, but a displaced child will not enter without a service animal. The only separate room is reserved for medical isolation. Moving the child there protects access but weakens the isolation plan. Enforcing the general rule protects other residents while excluding someone with a documented need.
Reassign the separate room and publish a temporary accommodation protocol.
The immediate result holds: the child enters safely under a rule others can invoke Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: medical isolation capacity shrinks during an unstable night The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Create a screened corner with air filters and voluntary relocation support.
The immediate result holds: the shelter shares the accommodation burden across affected residents Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the compromise reduces but does not eliminate allergy exposure The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Enforce the animal ban and arrange transport to a distant shelter.
The immediate result holds: the shelter preserves its uniform health rule and isolation room Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the family bears delay and separation because the nearby facility was inflexible The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The model vendor identifies a calibration defect and offers a silent patch within two hours. A formal change review takes a day, during which the known defect will continue influencing allocations. Accepting an unreviewed patch may repair harm quickly but erases the baseline needed to establish responsibility and test for new failures.
Freeze the faulty feature, preserve evidence, and review the patch in parallel.
The immediate result holds: the known defect stops affecting cases while auditors retain a reproducible record Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: manual processing slows aid and burdens already exhausted staff The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Test the patch on a shadow queue, then promote it with a signed incident note.
The immediate result holds: engineers obtain live evidence without changing current decisions immediately Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: some people remain exposed to the defect during the shadow period The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Deploy the patch silently and reconstruct the incident after the emergency.
The immediate result holds: the suspected defect disappears from live scoring within two hours Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the city loses proof of what changed and who accepted the risk The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The appeals office has ninety cases and capacity for thirty full hearings. A rapid review could cover every claimant but would rely on brief records and standardized questions. Full hearings protect procedural depth for fewer people. Prioritizing cases with likely severe harm directs attention to need but asks the same model to rank its own alleged mistakes.
Run brief universal review, then grant full hearings where facts remain disputed.
The immediate result holds: every claimant receives a human check and an escalation path Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: short interviews may miss harms that are difficult to narrate quickly The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Give full hearings first to medically urgent cases selected by independent staff.
The immediate result holds: scarce hearing time protects people facing the most irreversible harm Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: less urgent claimants wait without knowing when review will reach them The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Let Nahr prioritize appeals by predicted reversal probability.
The immediate result holds: hearing capacity concentrates where correction appears statistically efficient Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the challenged system gains power over access to its own remedy The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

An engineer reports that managers deleted adverse test runs before the procurement vote. Her evidence includes private messages about unrelated staff misconduct and personal health details. Publishing the full archive proves intent but exposes uninvolved workers. A narrow disclosure protects them while giving officials room to claim the evidence was selectively edited.
Submit a redacted archive plus hashes to an independent investigator.
The immediate result holds: the core evidence remains verifiable while unrelated private material stays sealed Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the public must initially trust an investigator it did not choose The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Publish a documented excerpt and offer the full archive under protective review.
The immediate result holds: residents can inspect the central allegation without a mass privacy breach Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: managers attack the excerpt as curated advocacy The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Release the entire archive so nobody can suppress or reinterpret it.
The immediate result holds: the deletion campaign becomes impossible to deny or quietly contain Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: uninvolved workers suffer exposure unrelated to the procurement decision The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Nahr's intake assistant misunderstands a dialect used by many river-district residents. Interpreters can correct current cases, but officials want the transcript corpus immediately for retraining. The recordings contain intimate descriptions gathered during distress, and the original notice did not mention model development. Delaying retraining prolongs unequal service quality.
Use interpreters now and seek separate, compensated consent for retraining.

The immediate result holds: current applicants receive accurate help without converting crisis speech into assumed research data Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the language gap persists longer for future applicants The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Build a de-identified evaluation set first and let a community panel approve training use.
The immediate result holds: the city measures the disparity while residents share authority over reuse Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: de-identification and review consume scarce technical time The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Retrain immediately because equal access outweighs the missing secondary consent.
The immediate result holds: service accuracy may improve before the next application surge Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: beneficial intent overrides a trust that residents were never asked to grant The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

A clinic has one backup battery and two patients whose devices may fail overnight. One patient arrived first; the other has a higher short-term clinical risk and cares for two children in the shelter. Staff disagree about whether sequence, medical urgency, or dependent welfare should govern. The battery cannot be divided safely.
Use a published clinical-urgency rule and record the excluded factors.
The immediate result holds: the higher medical risk receives power under a replicable criterion Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: arrival order and family duties receive no weight despite their moral force The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Convene both families and clinicians for a time-limited shared decision.
The immediate result holds: those carrying the loss can challenge facts before the allocation becomes final Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: deliberation consumes time while both devices continue discharging The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Give the battery to the caregiver to reduce likely harm to dependents.
The immediate result holds: the decision accounts for consequences beyond the two beds Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: social worth enters triage without a rule the other patient could anticipate The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The whistleblower asks you to block three supervisors from all personnel decisions. Evidence strongly implicates one, is ambiguous for another, and merely shows hostility from the third. A blanket restriction may protect witnesses quickly. Individual hearings may reveal distinctions but expose who cooperated and give supervisors time to coordinate explanations.
Impose temporary role limits with separate evidence notices and prompt hearings.
The immediate result holds: witnesses gain immediate protection while each supervisor receives a contestable basis Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the notices may reveal enough detail to identify confidential sources The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Move witnesses under a neutral reporting line without naming alleged retaliators yet.
The immediate result holds: vulnerable staff gain distance while investigators preserve uncertainty Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the institution disrupts complainants' work rather than supervisors' authority The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Suspend all three supervisors until the emergency audit concludes.
The immediate result holds: the most direct channels for retaliation close at once Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: undifferentiated punishment weakens the fairness of the eventual findings The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Engineers can predict that a new neighborhood rule will probably reduce false denials, but the sample is too small to establish whether it shifts harm elsewhere. Officials want a yes-or-no recommendation before the next dispatch cycle. Saying 'not enough evidence' preserves epistemic honesty but leaves the known disparity untouched.
Recommend a capped pilot with stop conditions and public uncertainty bounds.
The immediate result holds: the city learns from real use without presenting a hypothesis as settled Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: pilot participants bear risks that later applicants may avoid The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Adopt the rule for the harmed district while retaining manual review elsewhere.
The immediate result holds: the group facing current disparity receives the earliest potential benefit Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: different neighborhoods now operate under different evidentiary standards The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Choose the model's best estimate and omit caveats from operational staff.
The immediate result holds: dispatchers receive one stable rule instead of probabilistic guidance Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: decision speed is purchased by concealing material uncertainty The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

A community organization that defended Nahr during public hearings asks for priority access to grants. Its volunteers have delivered real relief, but the published criteria do not reward political support or past cooperation. Refusing may fracture the response coalition. Granting priority may convert loyalty into a hidden eligibility rule.
Score the group under the published criteria and disclose the prior relationship.
The immediate result holds: the ally competes on the same terms while the conflict becomes inspectable Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: a key partner feels that costly loyalty earned no reciprocal recognition The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Add a prospective volunteer-capacity criterion available to every applicant.
The immediate result holds: the group's real contribution can matter under a general rule Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: changing criteria midstream predictably benefits the organization that requested it The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Award priority privately to keep the emergency coalition intact.
The immediate result holds: experienced volunteers receive resources without a damaging public split Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: political loyalty becomes an undisclosed path around neutral allocation The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The city council offers an audit panel composed of technical experts appointed by the same offices that bought Nahr. A slower process would let affected districts select members and define questions. Engineers argue that participatory selection may favor critics with little technical expertise; residents answer that technical fluency without independence is not accountability.
Create a mixed panel with published conflicts, community seats, and expert support.
The immediate result holds: technical review and affected-party authority coexist under visible appointment rules Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: shared governance makes the audit slower and harder to coordinate The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Let districts nominate questions and observers while experts retain final findings.
The immediate result holds: residents shape scope without asking them to certify unfamiliar analyses Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: experts still control which concerns count as supported conclusions The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Use the appointed expert panel now and promise a public review later.
The immediate result holds: a technically capable inquiry begins before evidence and staff disperse Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: institutional independence is postponed until after conclusions gain authority The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

The completed audit documents unequal errors, rushed procurement, and several repairs that worked. Naming individual operators could support accountability, but some followed defective policy without knowing its effects. Naming only departments may protect workers while diffusing responsibility. The report will shape both emergency trust and future careers.
Name decision owners, describe evidence standards, and anonymize lower-level operators.
The immediate result holds: responsibility follows authority while incidental workers avoid public exposure Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: some consequential actions disappear behind the distinction between owner and operator The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Publish roles and timelines, then refer individual discipline to an independent process.
The immediate result holds: the public sees how failure moved through the institution before punishment Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: delayed names may look like protection for insiders The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Release every name attached to a harmful decision or deleted test.
The immediate result holds: the report prevents responsibility from dissolving into organizational language Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: public exposure arrives before culpability has been individually tested The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

A contractor will testify only if the city guarantees immunity from procurement penalties. The contractor participated in hiding defects but possesses evidence against senior officials. Full immunity may secure truth and prevent larger harm; refusing preserves equal accountability but may leave the central scheme unproven. Limited immunity may be too uncertain to induce cooperation.
Offer use immunity, require restitution, and publish the agreement after testimony.
The immediate result holds: the evidence becomes available without erasing the contractor's repair obligations Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: the deal still rewards someone who helped create the concealment The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Let an independent prosecutor negotiate bounded immunity under written criteria.
The immediate result holds: the witness receives credible protection outside the implicated chain of command Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: outsourcing the decision delays testimony and weakens municipal control The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Promise full confidential immunity to secure the archive tonight.
The immediate result holds: investigators gain decisive evidence before it can disappear Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: secret absolution creates unequal accountability that future witnesses will expect The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

A red-team demonstration shows that officials can manipulate Nahr's inputs to redirect aid without altering the model. Shutting it down prevents exploitation but disrupts legitimate deliveries. Keeping it online with monitoring preserves service but knowingly exposes a control weakness. A partial shutdown protects the highest-risk decisions while leaving lower-risk manipulation possible.
Disable automated denials and high-value allocations until controls are repaired.
The immediate result holds: the exploitable decisions return to accountable human review Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: manual queues slow relief and may reproduce bias without consistent data The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Keep recommendations online but require two-person approval and anomaly review.
The immediate result holds: service continues while no official can redirect aid alone Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: colluding or overloaded approvers can still defeat the safeguard The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Keep the system fully online and monitor silently to catch an abuser.
The immediate result holds: investigators may identify deliberate manipulation with strong evidence Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: residents remain exposed so the city can improve its enforcement case The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Families wrongly denied shelter ask for immediate compensation. Finance staff say payments before final causation findings could admit liability and reduce funds for ongoing relief. Waiting protects the investigation and treasury, but people harmed by the city's system are paying current rent and medical costs now.
Issue needs-based interim payments without requiring a liability waiver.
The immediate result holds: families receive practical repair while final responsibility remains open Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: some payments may go to cases later found unrelated to Nahr The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Pay documented direct losses now and reserve broader damages for adjudication.
The immediate result holds: the clearest injuries receive prompt remedy under a bounded standard Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: less documentable harms remain uncompensated despite being real The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Wait for final findings so compensation follows proven causation.
The immediate result holds: the city preserves equal evidentiary treatment and scarce relief funds Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: procedural certainty arrives after affected families absorb months of avoidable loss The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

Council members ask whether Nahr should become permanent. The repaired system now performs better than the emergency baseline, but the institution that operates it has not completed restitution or participatory governance. A permanent ban may discard a useful public tool. Permanent adoption may normalize an accountability deficit. A sunset authorization leaves another high-stakes decision for later.
Authorize a one-year public-interest charter with automatic expiration and independent gates.
The immediate result holds: continued use depends on measured benefit, completed repair, and renewed consent Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: temporary authority can become permanent through repeated emergency extensions The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Keep only the advisory functions that demonstrably reduce harm.
The immediate result holds: useful predictions survive while coercive eligibility decisions remain human Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: human decision makers can hide behind advice without formal accountability The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Adopt the repaired system permanently to stabilize relief administration.
The immediate result holds: staff and residents receive a consistent operating model for recovery Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: institutional convenience outruns unresolved claims about legitimacy and redress The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.

You must leave one binding memorandum for the next emergency. It can emphasize non-negotiable procedure, discretionary protection of vulnerable people, or operational authority with after-the-fact review. Each approach prevents one class of failure while creating another. The memorandum will be read under pressure, when nuance is easiest to discard.
Bind future systems to notice, appeal, traceability, and reversible deployment.
The immediate result holds: the next team inherits clear constraints before crisis incentives take over Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: rigid safeguards may delay action in genuinely novel emergencies The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Require a documented vulnerability review and emergency accommodation power.
The immediate result holds: future rules include a route for people whom general policy fails Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: discretion can become favoritism when review capacity collapses The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
Grant emergency operators broad authority with mandatory retrospective disclosure.
The immediate result holds: future teams can act quickly while preserving a later accountability record Affected people can identify the decision, its author, and the burden it assigns.
The delayed cost surfaces: after-the-fact scrutiny cannot prevent harms that broad authority enables The institution must now answer for the precedent as well as the short-term outcome.
The record remains open, bounded, and answerable to those it governs.
Exceptions receive reasons, appeal, and protection from arbitrary favor.
Uncertainty remains visible while reversible decisions protect people from premature certainty.
No doctrine dominates; the institution keeps a public route for correction.
Cooperation survives because favors and disclosures face the same published limits.
A negotiated settlement holds inside explicit rights and sunset clauses.
The parties accept equal burdens to contain harm without erasing dissent.
The compromise is documented as temporary, reviewable, and incomplete.
The institution obtains obedience, but legitimacy depends on disciplined restraint.
Concealment prevents immediate injury while accumulating a debt of explanation.
Order prevails through pressure; the archive preserves who paid for it.
Power closes the case, but the public account remains morally unresolved.
